output.brief: The likeliest cause of the rise in delayed alarm responses is the 12 August relay server move. The new server dropped 11 of 14 forwarding rules, so the 15-second SpO2 hold-off, repeat-alarm suppression and technical-alarm routing were lost. Phone notifications per nurse roughly doubled from that date in Pods A-C, and response times and incidents rose with them. Pod D still uses the old server and shows no change, which is the key control. Agency share and patient acuity do not explain the pattern: Pod D has similar agency use with no rise, and alarm volume was flat. Confidence is moderate-to-good; the logs show dispatch, not handset receipt, and I did not check the wireless gap or the monitor update. Next steps: have Clinical Engineering validate and restore the forwarding rules (A1), with weekly tracking. Do not approve the agency cap or nurse reviews, which punish staff for a system fault. Do not stop phone alarms (A3) in the meantime. Confirm handset delivery before closing the case.
